title: Stream values that may be null without tripping over them

blocks.text: `Stream.of((String) null)` is **not** an empty stream: it holds one `null` element. `Stream.ofNullable(value)` (Java 9) is the null-safe tap: empty for `null`, a one-element stream otherwise. And `Arrays.stream(array)` on a `null` array throws, so a source that may be `null` must be guarded before it is streamed.

items: `nicknames(List<NullSafe.Person> people)` returns the nicknames of the people, in their order. A `Person(String name, String nickname)` may have a `null` nickname; such a person contributes nothing. Every other nickname is listed, even an empty one, and a repeated one each time.
`countItems(String[] items)` returns how many slots the array has, `null` entries included; a `null` array holds none.

blocks.text: Neither method throws on a `null`, and neither lets one into its answer.

cases.says: It lists every nickname in order and counts the items of an array.
A missing nickname adds nothing: Stream.ofNullable(null) is empty, while Stream.of((String) null) holds one null.
A null array counts zero items instead of throwing NullPointerException.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Streaming a null array or collection throws, so a source that may be null is guarded first.
Stream.ofNullable gives an empty stream for null, while Stream.of((T) null) gives a stream holding one null.
